terrestrial

/tuh-RES-tree-uhl/ — rhymes with celestial · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Terrestrial describes something relating to the earth or land, as opposed to water, air, or space.

Unlike its water-loving cousins, this terrestrial crab lives its whole life on land.

Example

The naturalist separated the creatures into two categories: the aquatic species that thrived in the pond, and the terrestrial species that lived in the surrounding grassland.

Terrestrial is more precise than 'land-based' or 'ground-dwelling' because it's the scientific term that contrasts specifically with aquatic (water) and aerial (air) environments, giving biology a standard classification.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

land-based: Land-based is the everyday label for machines, buildings, and operations that work on land — a land-based telescope, land-based transport. Terrestrial does the same job for nature: it is the biologist's term for land creatures, the standard scientific contrast with life in the water or the air.

ground-dwelling: Ground-dwelling picks out exactly where an animal spends its time: on the ground itself, not up in the branches or under water. Terrestrial is broader — a tree squirrel is still a terrestrial animal, because terrestrial covers all life on land, from the canopy to the forest floor.

earthbound: Earthbound means unable to leave the earth, and its contrast is with flying and with space — a grounded rocket is earthbound, and so is a bird with a clipped wing. Terrestrial contrasts with water instead: a terrestrial animal is one whose life is built for dry land.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

aquatic: living or growing in the water

celestial: relating to the sky or heavens, not the earth

Where it sits · where the creature lives, water to land

aquatic → amphibious → arboreal → terrestrial

aquatic vs. terrestrial: Aquatic is the opposite end from terrestrial: an aquatic creature lives in water, while a terrestrial one lives on dry land.

amphibious vs. terrestrial: Amphibious sits between the two extremes, since an amphibious animal can live both in water and on land, whereas a terrestrial animal is suited to land alone.

arboreal vs. terrestrial: Arboreal is more specific than terrestrial: an arboreal animal lives up in the trees, while terrestrial simply means living on the ground or land in general.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — terr(a): earth, land (Latin)

Suffix — -estrial: characteristic of (a stretched form of -ial) (Latin)

Put it together: The Latin root terra means 'earth, land,' and the stretched ending -estrial carries the -ial sense of 'characteristic of.' Put together, terrestrial means 'characteristic of the earth or land' — describing life that belongs on the ground rather than in water, air, or space.

Use the root in a new word: extraterrestrial: In the movie, an extraterrestrial crash-lands in a farmer's cornfield — the terr- of terrestrial sits right in the middle of its name.

Root Check

Word Choice

scientific / formal

Use terrestrial when you need a scientific or formal way to describe something relating to land. In everyday speech, you might say 'land animal' or 'ground-dwelling,' but terrestrial is the technical term biologists use to contrast with aquatic and aerial.
